steps.text: Heat the coconut oil in a kadai, pop the mustard seeds, then add red chillies, hing and curry leaves.
steps.visual: Mustard seeds, broken red chillies and curry leaves crackling in coconut oil in a black iron kadai

steps.title: Toss with coconut
steps.text: Add the boiled peanuts and toss for 2 minutes. Turn off the heat, add the coconut and a squeeze of lemon if you like.
steps.visual: Boiled peanuts tossed with white coconut, mustard seeds and curry leaves in the black iron kadai

steps.title: Serve
steps.text: Serve warm in small bowls or paper cones.
steps.visual: A paper cone filled with peanut sundal flecked with coconut and curry leaves, more in a small steel bowl

substitutions.note: For a peanut-allergy-safe sundal use chickpeas instead.

recipes.reheating: Eat at room temperature or warm briefly in a pan.

recipes.title: Thayir Sadam (Curd Rice)
recipes.description: Soft, creamy Tamil curd rice: well-cooked rice mashed with curd and a little milk, tempered with mustard, urad dal, ginger, green chilli and curry leaves, with grated cucumber.

steps.title: Cook the rice soft
steps.text: Wash the rice and pressure-cook it with the water for 4 whistles, about 15 minutes, so it is very soft. Curd rice needs softer rice than usual.
steps.visual: Very soft, sticky cooked white rice in an open steel pressure cooker

steps.title: Mash and cool
steps.text: Transfer the hot rice to a bowl and mash it well with a ladle. Let it cool until just warm, about 10 minutes — adding curd to hot rice makes it sour quickly.
steps.visual: Mashed, creamy white rice in a wide steel mixing bowl, a ladle resting across it

steps.title: Mix in the curd
steps.text: Add the curd, milk and salt and mix until creamy. Stir in the grated cucumber. The milk keeps the curd rice from turning too sour if packed for later.
steps.visual: Creamy, loose white curd rice with flecks of pale green cucumber in the steel mixing bowl

steps.title: Temper
steps.text: Heat the oil in a small kadai. Pop the mustard seeds, then add urad dal and fry until golden. Add ginger, green chilli, curry leaves and hing and stir for 20 seconds.
steps.visual: Golden urad dal, popped mustard seeds, chopped ginger, green chilli and curry leaves sizzling in a small black kadai

steps.title: Combine
steps.text: Pour the tempering over the curd rice, add the coriander and mix well.
steps.visual: Mustard seeds, curry leaves and coriander streaked through the creamy curd rice in the steel mixing bowl

steps.title: Serve
steps.text: Serve at room temperature or slightly chilled with a spicy pickle, vatha kuzhambu or a poriyal.
steps.visual: A mound of creamy white thayir sadam on a banana leaf topped with curry leaves and mustard seeds, a little red pickle and beetroot poriyal beside

substitutions.note: Little millet (samai) makes a lighter curd rice with more fibre.
Grated carrot or pomegranate are popular additions.

recipes.storage: Refrigerate up to 1 day; add a splash of milk before packing.
recipes.reheating: Served cold or at room temperature — loosen with a little milk or curd.

recipes.title: Elumichai Sadam (Lemon Rice)
recipes.description: Tangy, turmeric-yellow lemon rice tossed with a crunchy tempering of peanuts, chana and urad dal, green chilli, ginger and curry leaves. A classic Tamil lunch-box rice.

steps.title: Cook and cool the rice
steps.text: Wash the rice and pressure-cook it with the water for 3 whistles, about 12 minutes, so the grains stay separate. Spread on a plate to cool for 10 minutes.
steps.visual: Fluffy, separate white rice grains spread out to cool on a wide steel plate

steps.title: Fry the dals and peanuts
steps.text: Heat the oil in a wide kadai. Pop the mustard seeds, then add chana dal, urad dal and peanuts and fry on medium-low heat until golden and crunchy, about 2 minutes.
steps.visual: Golden peanuts, chana dal and urad dal with popped mustard seeds in oil in a wide black iron kadai

steps.title: Add the aromatics
steps.text: Add the red chillies, green chillies, ginger, curry leaves and hing and stir for 30 seconds. Turn off the heat and stir in the turmeric and salt.
steps.visual: Bright yellow turmeric-tinged oil with crunchy dals, peanuts, chillies and curry leaves in the wide black iron kadai

steps.title: Add lemon juice
steps.text: With the heat off, pour in the lemon juice and mix. Adding lemon off the heat keeps it from turning bitter.
steps.visual: Lemon juice being squeezed into the yellow tempering in the wide black iron kadai

steps.title: Toss the rice
steps.text: Add the cooled rice and gently fold until every grain is yellow. Add the coriander and rest for 10 minutes so the rice absorbs the flavour.
steps.visual: Bright yellow rice grains evenly coated and studded with peanuts and curry leaves in the wide black iron kadai

steps.title: Serve
steps.text: Serve with a vegetable poriyal, egg podimas or a cup of curd to round out the meal.
steps.visual: A mound of yellow lemon rice with peanuts and curry leaves on a banana leaf, a lemon wedge and beans poriyal beside

substitutions.note: Cooked foxtail millet makes a lighter lemon 'rice' with more fibre.
Cashews for a festive version, or skip nuts for a nut-free rice.

recipes.storage: Keeps well at room temperature for 6 hours in a lunch box; refrigerate up to 1 day.
recipes.reheating: Sprinkle with water and microwave for 1 minute, or eat at room temperature.

recipes.title: Coconut Chutney
recipes.description: The essential tiffin chutney: fresh coconut ground with roasted gram, green chilli and ginger, finished with a mustard, urad dal and curry leaf tempering in coconut oil.

steps.title: Gather the chutney ingredients
steps.text: Put the grated coconut, roasted gram, green chillies, ginger and salt into a mixer jar.
steps.visual: Snowy grated coconut, pale yellow roasted gram, two green chillies and a piece of ginger inside a steel mixer jar

steps.title: Grind smooth
steps.text: Add the water a little at a time and grind to a smooth, thick chutney that just drops from a spoon. Scrape into a bowl.
steps.visual: Smooth, thick, creamy white coconut chutney in a steel bowl with green chilli flecks

steps.title: Temper
steps.text: Heat the coconut oil in a small kadai. Add the mustard seeds; when they pop add urad dal, red chilli and curry leaves and fry until the dal is golden.
steps.visual: Popping mustard seeds, golden urad dal, a red chilli and curry leaves in coconut oil in a small black kadai

steps.title: Finish and serve
steps.text: Pour the tempering over the chutney. Serve with idli, dosa, adai, pongal or paniyaram.
steps.visual: White coconut chutney in a small steel bowl topped with popped mustard seeds, curry leaves and a red chilli, beside a dosa

substitutions.note: Roasted peanuts can replace roasted gram; or skip it for a lower-carb chutney.
Red chillies give a pink-tinged, smokier chutney.

recipes.storage: Refrigerate up to 1 day; coconut chutney turns sour quickly at room temperature.
recipes.reheating: Serve cold or at room temperature; do not heat.

recipes.title: Tomato Chutney
recipes.description: A tangy, spicy tomato chutney of ripe tomatoes and onion cooked down with red chillies, garlic and roasted urad and chana dal, then ground and tempered.

steps.title: Roast the dals and chillies
steps.text: Heat 2 teaspoons of the oil in a kadai on medium-low heat. Fry the urad dal, chana dal and red chillies until the dals are golden, about 2 minutes.
steps.visual: Golden urad and chana dal with dark red chillies frying in a little oil in a black iron kadai

steps.title: Cook onion and garlic
steps.text: Add the garlic and onion and sauté for 3 minutes until the onion is soft.
steps.visual: Softened chopped onion and garlic cloves with the roasted dals and chillies in the black iron kadai

steps.title: Cook down the tomatoes
steps.text: Add the tomatoes, tamarind if using, and salt. Cook for 7 to 8 minutes, stirring, until the tomatoes collapse into a thick, jammy mass.
steps.visual: Collapsed, jammy red tomatoes cooked down with onion and chillies in the black iron kadai

steps.title: Cool and grind
steps.text: Cool the mixture completely and grind it to a slightly coarse chutney without adding water.
steps.visual: Thick, coarse, deep orange-red chutney in a mixer jar

steps.title: Temper
steps.text: Heat the remaining oil in the kadai, pop the mustard seeds, add curry leaves and hing and pour over the chutney.
steps.visual: Sizzling mustard seeds and curry leaves in the black iron kadai being poured over the red chutney

steps.title: Serve
steps.text: Serve with idli, dosa, egg dosa, adai or paniyaram.
steps.visual: A small steel bowl of glossy red tomato chutney topped with mustard seeds and curry leaves beside soft idlis

substitutions.note: Kashmiri chilli powder gives a brighter colour with less heat for children.
Use gluten-free hing if needed.

recipes.reheating: Serve at room temperature.

recipes.title: Pudina Thogayal
recipes.description: A thick, coarse mint thogayal ground with roasted urad dal, red chillies, tamarind and coconut. Mixed into hot rice with gingelly oil or served with dosa.

steps.title: Roast the urad dal
steps.text: Heat the gingelly oil in a kadai on low heat. Fry the urad dal and red chillies until the dal is deep golden, about 2 minutes, then add the hing.
steps.visual: Deep golden urad dal and dark red chillies frying in gingelly oil in a black iron kadai

steps.title: Wilt the mint
steps.text: Add the mint and coriander leaves and sauté for 2 minutes until just wilted. Add the tamarind and coconut and stir for a minute. Turn off the heat and cool.
steps.visual: Wilted dark green mint and coriander leaves with coconut and a piece of tamarind among the golden dal in the black iron kadai

steps.title: Grind coarsely
steps.text: Grind the cooled mixture with the salt and just enough water to a thick, coarse paste — thogayal should be thicker than chutney.
steps.visual: Thick, coarse, dark green thogayal with visible bits of dal in a mixer jar

steps.title: Serve
steps.text: Serve with hot rice and a drizzle of gingelly oil, or with dosa, idli and curd rice.
steps.visual: A small mound of thick, dark green pudina thogayal on a banana leaf next to hot rice with a drizzle of oil

substitutions.note: Leave out the coconut for a longer-keeping thogayal (up to 5 days).
Chana dal gives a nuttier, slightly sweeter thogayal.

recipes.reheating: Serve at room temperature.

recipes.title: Peerkangai Thogayal (Ridge Gourd Thogayal)
recipes.description: Ridge gourd sautéed with garlic and ground with roasted urad dal, red chillies and tamarind into a thick, mildly sweet and spicy thogayal.

steps.title: Prepare the ridge gourd
steps.text: Wash the ridge gourd, scrape off just the hard ridges with a peeler and chop into small pieces. Taste a sliver — discard it if bitter.
steps.visual: Chopped pale green ridge gourd pieces on a wooden board, scraped ridges in a small pile beside

steps.title: Roast dal and chillies
steps.text: Heat 1 teaspoon of the oil in a kadai on low heat. Fry the urad dal and red chillies until the dal is golden, then add the hing and lift out.
steps.visual: Golden urad dal and red chillies in a little oil in a black iron kadai

steps.title: Sauté the ridge gourd
steps.text: In the same kadai sauté the garlic for 30 seconds, then add the ridge gourd and tamarind. Cook uncovered on medium heat for 7 to 8 minutes until soft and most of the water has evaporated. Cool.
steps.visual: Soft, translucent ridge gourd pieces with garlic and a piece of tamarind in the black iron kadai, little liquid left

steps.title: Grind
steps.text: First grind the roasted dal and chillies coarsely, then add the cooked ridge gourd and salt and pulse to a thick, slightly coarse thogayal. No water is needed.
steps.visual: Thick, coarse olive-green thogayal flecked with red chilli in a mixer jar

steps.title: Temper
steps.text: Heat the remaining oil in the kadai, pop the mustard seeds, add curry leaves and pour over the thogayal.
steps.visual: Popping mustard seeds and curry leaves in the black iron kadai being poured over the green thogayal

steps.title: Serve
steps.text: Serve with hot rice and ghee, curd rice, or dosa.
steps.visual: A small steel bowl of olive-green peerkangai thogayal topped with mustard seeds and curry leaves beside curd rice

substitutions.note: Bottle gourd makes a similar mild thogayal.
Skip the garlic for a no-onion-garlic version; add a little extra hing.

recipes.reheating: Serve at room temperature.

recipes.title: Kara Chutney
recipes.description: Fiery Chettinad-style red chutney of shallots, dried red chillies, garlic, a little tomato and tamarind cooked in gingelly oil — the perfect partner for paniyaram and idli.

steps.title: Fry the chillies
steps.text: Heat 2 teaspoons of the gingelly oil in a kadai on low heat. Fry the dried red chillies for 30 seconds until they puff and darken slightly.
steps.visual: Puffed, glossy dark red chillies in gingelly oil in a black iron kadai

steps.title: Sauté shallots and garlic
steps.text: Add the shallots and garlic and sauté on medium heat for 5 minutes until soft and lightly browned.
steps.visual: Soft, golden-edged whole shallots and garlic cloves with the red chillies in the black iron kadai

steps.title: Add tomato and tamarind
steps.text: Add the tomato, tamarind and salt and cook for 3 to 4 minutes until the tomato is soft. Cool completely.
steps.visual: Soft tomato pieces and tamarind among the shallots and chillies in the black iron kadai

steps.title: Grind
steps.text: Grind to a smooth, thick paste with 2 to 3 tablespoons of water.
steps.visual: A thick, smooth, brick-red chutney in a mixer jar

steps.title: Temper
steps.text: Heat the remaining oil in the kadai, pop the mustard seeds, then add urad dal, curry leaves and hing. Add the ground chutney and cook for 2 minutes on low heat until it darkens slightly and the oil rises.
steps.visual: Deep red chutney bubbling gently in the black iron kadai with oil glistening at the edges and mustard seeds on top

steps.title: Serve
steps.text: Serve with kuzhi paniyaram, idli, dosa or adai. A little goes a long way.
steps.visual: A small stone bowl of glossy deep red kara chutney with curry leaves on top beside golden kuzhi paniyarams

substitutions.note: Onion works but shallots give the classic sweetness and colour.
Use Kashmiri chilli powder for colour with less heat.

recipes.reheating: Serve at room temperature.

recipes.title: Murungai Keerai Poriyal
recipes.description: Drumstick (moringa) leaves stir-fried with shallots, a little soaked moong dal and red chilli, finished with fresh coconut. Earthy, slightly bitter and full of flavour.

steps.title: Strip and soak
steps.text: Strip the tiny drumstick leaves from their stems, discarding any yellow leaves. Wash in plenty of water and drain. Soak the moong dal in water for 30 minutes.
steps.visual: A heap of tiny bright green moringa leaves in a colander beside a small bowl of soaking yellow moong dal, bare stems on the board

steps.title: Temper
steps.text: Heat the coconut oil in a kadai. Add mustard seeds; when they pop add urad dal and red chillies and fry until golden.
steps.visual: Popping mustard seeds, golden urad dal and red chilli pieces in coconut oil in a black iron kadai

steps.title: Sauté shallots and dal
steps.text: Add the shallots and sauté for 2 minutes. Add the drained moong dal and turmeric and stir for a minute.
steps.visual: Soft pink shallots and soaked yellow moong dal with the tempering in the black iron kadai

steps.title: Cook the leaves
steps.text: Add the drumstick leaves, salt and water. Cover and cook on low heat for 5 to 6 minutes, stirring once, until the leaves are tender and the dal is cooked but still holds its shape.
steps.visual: Wilted dark green moringa leaves with yellow dal in the covered black iron kadai, steam escaping as the lid lifts

steps.title: Add coconut
steps.text: Uncover, cook off any remaining water and toss in the grated coconut.
steps.visual: White grated coconut being folded into the dark green moringa leaves in the black iron kadai

steps.title: Serve
steps.text: Serve warm with rice and sambar or rasam.
steps.visual: A steel bowl of dark green murungai keerai poriyal flecked with coconut, yellow dal and red chilli beside rasam and rice

substitutions.note: Any keerai can be made the same way; amaranth needs a little more volume.
Skip the dal for a lighter, lower-carb poriyal.

recipes.reheating: Warm briefly in a pan.

recipes.title: Ash Gourd Mor Kootu
recipes.description: Soft ash gourd and moong dal in a mild, creamy curd and coconut–green chilli–cumin sauce, finished with a coconut-oil tempering. A cooling kootu for hot days.

steps.title: Cook the dal
steps.text: Simmer the moong dal with 1 cup of water and the turmeric in a saucepan for 12 minutes until soft.
steps.visual: Soft yellow moong dal simmering in a steel saucepan

steps.title: Cook the ash gourd
steps.text: Add the ash gourd cubes, salt and ½ cup of water. Cover and cook for 7 to 8 minutes until the ash gourd turns translucent and soft.
steps.visual: Translucent, pale green ash gourd cubes in yellow dal in the covered steel saucepan

steps.title: Grind the coconut paste
steps.text: Grind the coconut, green chilli and cumin with 3 tablespoons of water to a smooth paste.
steps.visual: Smooth, creamy white coconut and green chilli paste in a small mixer jar

steps.title: Simmer with the paste
steps.text: Stir the coconut paste into the saucepan and simmer for 3 minutes. Turn the heat to the lowest setting.
steps.visual: Thick, pale kootu with ash gourd cubes gently bubbling in the steel saucepan

steps.title: Add the curd
steps.text: Take the pan off the heat for a minute, then stir in the whisked curd. Return to very low heat and warm for 1 minute, stirring — don't let it boil or the curd will split.
steps.visual: Creamy white mor kootu with ash gourd cubes in the steel saucepan, curd stirred through smoothly

steps.title: Temper
steps.text: Heat the coconut oil in a small kadai, pop the mustard seeds, add the red chilli and curry leaves and pour over the kootu.
steps.visual: Popping mustard seeds, a red chilli and curry leaves in coconut oil being poured over the creamy kootu

steps.title: Serve
steps.text: Serve warm or at room temperature with rice and a spicy poriyal or fish fry.
steps.visual: A steel bowl of creamy white ash gourd mor kootu topped with mustard seeds, curry leaves and a red chilli, rice beside

substitutions.note: Chow chow makes an equally classic mor kootu.
For a dairy-free version, finish with thick coconut milk and a squeeze of lemon instead of curd.

recipes.reheating: Warm on very low heat without boiling.

recipes.title: Chettinad Kara Kuzhi Paniyaram
recipes.description: Savoury rice and urad dal dumplings from Chettinad, made with fermented batter and a tempering of shallots, green chilli, ginger and coconut, cooked crisp in a paniyaram pan.

steps.title: Soak rice and dal
steps.text: Wash the rice and soak it for 4 hours. Separately soak the urad dal with the fenugreek seeds for the same time.
steps.visual: Two steel bowls, one with parboiled rice and one with urad dal and fenugreek seeds, both soaking in water

steps.title: Grind the batter
steps.text: Grind the urad dal until fluffy, then the rice until slightly grainy. Mix both with the salt and enough water to make a thick batter, thicker than idli batter.
steps.visual: Thick, off-white batter with a fine grainy texture in a large steel mixing bowl

steps.title: Ferment
steps.text: Cover and ferment in a warm place for 8 hours or overnight until risen and slightly sour.
steps.visual: The steel bowl of batter risen with bubbles on the surface

steps.title: Make the tempering
steps.text: Heat 2 teaspoons of the oil in a small kadai. Pop the mustard seeds, then add chana dal and fry until golden. Add curry leaves, shallots, green chilli and ginger and sauté for 2 minutes. Stir in the coconut.
steps.visual: Soft chopped shallots, green chilli, ginger, golden chana dal, curry leaves and white coconut in a small black kadai

steps.title: Mix into the batter
steps.text: Stir the tempering into the fermented batter.
steps.visual: Off-white batter in the steel bowl speckled with shallots, curry leaves, mustard seeds and coconut

steps.title: Fill the paniyaram pan
steps.text: Heat a paniyaram (kuzhi) pan over medium heat and add a few drops of oil to each cavity. Fill each cavity three-quarters full with batter.
steps.visual: A black paniyaram pan with each round cavity filled with speckled batter, oil sizzling at the edges

steps.title: Cook and turn
steps.text: Cover and cook for 3 minutes until the bottoms are golden. Turn each paniyaram with a skewer, add a drop more oil and cook for 2 minutes until golden all over. Repeat with the remaining batter.
steps.visual: Golden, round paniyarams being turned with a wooden skewer in the black paniyaram pan, crisp golden shells showing

steps.title: Serve
steps.text: Serve hot, about seven per person, with kara chutney, coconut chutney or tomato chutney.
steps.visual: A pile of golden, crisp kuzhi paniyarams on a banana leaf with bowls of red kara chutney and white coconut chutney

substitutions.note: Swap half or all of the rice for foxtail millet for a millet paniyaram.
Any neutral oil works.

recipes.storage: Fermented batter keeps 2 days refrigerated; cooked paniyarams are best fresh.
recipes.reheating: Re-crisp in the paniyaram pan or an air fryer at 170°C for 3 minutes.

recipes.title: Karuveppilai Chicken (Curry Leaf Chicken)
recipes.description: Boneless chicken roasted dry with a fragrant ground paste of fresh curry leaves, black pepper, fennel, cumin and garlic, finished with lemon. Deep green, peppery and aromatic.

steps.title: Roast the spices and leaves
steps.text: Dry-roast the pepper, fennel, cumin, coriander seeds and red chillies in a kadai on low heat for 2 minutes. Add three-quarters of the curry leaves and roast for 1 more minute until they turn crisp and dark green.
steps.visual: Crisp, dark green curry leaves with peppercorns, fennel, cumin, coriander seeds and red chillies roasting in a dry black iron kadai

steps.title: Grind the curry leaf paste
steps.text: Cool, then grind the roasted mixture with the garlic, ginger and 3 tablespoons of water to a thick, coarse green paste.
steps.visual: A thick, dark green, coarse curry leaf and pepper paste in a mixer jar

steps.title: Marinate the chicken
steps.text: Toss the chicken with the curry leaf paste, turmeric and salt in a bowl. Marinate for 20 minutes.
steps.visual: Boneless chicken pieces coated in a dark green paste in a steel mixing bowl

steps.title: Fry the shallots
steps.text: Heat the oil in the same kadai on medium heat. Add the remaining curry leaves and the shallots and sauté for 5 minutes until golden.
steps.visual: Golden sliced shallots and fresh curry leaves sizzling in oil in the black iron kadai

steps.title: Cook the chicken
steps.text: Add the marinated chicken and stir-fry on high heat for 3 minutes to sear. Lower the heat, cover and cook for 8 minutes, stirring once, until the chicken is cooked through.
steps.visual: Green-coated chicken pieces searing with shallots in the black iron kadai, juices starting to release

steps.title: Roast dry
steps.text: Uncover and roast on medium-high heat for 5 to 6 minutes, stirring often, until the chicken is dry, dark green-brown and the masala clings to every piece.
steps.visual: Dry, dark green-brown chicken pieces with crisp curry leaves and caramelised shallots in the black iron kadai

steps.title: Finish with lemon and serve
steps.text: Turn off the heat, squeeze over the lemon juice and toss. Serve hot with rasam and rice, chapati, or a salad and kootu.
steps.visual: Dark green curry leaf chicken heaped in a brass bowl with crisp curry leaves on top and a lemon wedge, rasam alongside

substitutions.note: Breast is leaner; reduce the covered cooking time to 6 minutes so it stays juicy.
Coconut oil pairs well with the curry leaf flavour.

recipes.reheating: Reheat in a hot pan with a splash of water.
